answer: Charge admission. Every new agent in the economy deposits a stake before its votes or attestations count, and the network slashes that stake when the agent is caught forging identity or double-spending trust. An attacker juggling a million wallets during a long voyage of consensus rounds must lock real capital in each one, so the cost of a sybil swarm grows linearly while its payoff stays fixed. Peers then publish a shared atlas of slashed identities, making rebirth expensive. Proof-of-work alone is an ivory gate that botnets walk through cheaply; priced identity is not.
